result.topic_en: Gauss expresses the electrodynamic interaction of two closed current curves as the variation of a double integral, gives a shorter proof of this, and lists several equivalent forms of the double integral.

1) $\delta\iint \varrho dd'\varrho = \iint \delta\varrho.\partial\partial'\varrho + \iint\varrho\,\delta\partial\partial'\varrho$
2) $\iint\varrho\,\partial' d\delta\varrho + \iint \partial'\varrho.d\delta\varrho = \iint\partial'(\varrho d\delta\varrho) = 0$
3) $0 = \iint\partial(\delta\varrho.\partial'\varrho) = \iint \partial'\varrho.\partial\delta\varrho + \iint\partial\partial'\varrho.\delta\varrho$
Also durch Addition

Das unter dem Variationszeichen stehende Doppelintegral
kann auf verschiedene Arten ausgedrückt werden
$\iint\varrho dd'\varrho = -\iint d\varrho.d'\varrho$
$= \frac{1}{4r}.\cos\theta.\cos\theta'$
$= \frac{1}{4r}.(\cos\theta.\cos\theta' + \sin\theta\sin\theta'\cos\omega)$
$= \frac{1}{2-m}\iint\varrho^{\frac{[-2m-m-]2-m}{m}[?]}.\,[-\partial\partial'-]\partial\partial'\varrho^m$
$= -\frac{1}{m}\iint\varrho^{\frac{2m-2m}{m}[?]}.\partial\varrho^m.\partial'\varrho^m$

methods.what: Interaction of two current curves written as minus the variation of the double integral of the product of line elements divided by distance (Neumann-type potential)
Shorter proof: variation of the double integral computed via integration by parts over the closed curves; adding three identities gives the result
Integration by parts over closed curves (total differentials integrate to zero)
Equivalent expressions of the double integral via integration by parts, angle forms and powers of rho
Equivalent form of the double integral in terms of the angles theta, theta' and omega
Equivalent form of the double integral in terms of the m-th power of rho
